Source findings and transition design (planning, not runtime verification)

Inspected authenticated live master `1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4`. The user's requested outcome is authoritative; the reported three-second timing differs from this source, and the installed/served version was not identified. No app run, implementation or test execution is claimed.

**Current contracts**

- [Core gesture](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/packages/core/src/interaction.ts#L91-L126) uses `PARENT_HOLD_MS = 2000`, monotonic readiness and release validation; movement over 12 units cancels. [useParentHold](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/useParentHold.ts) shares the clock/timer, generation invalidation and contact tracking. Existing native/core/browser tests already cover 1,999/2,000 ms, early timers, repeat attempts and several cancellations; extend these rather than replacing the gesture.
- [PlayBoard](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/PlayBoard.tsx) opens the exit sheet after ready release. The sheet blocks new card activation, but stopping audio currently occurs on confirmed exit. Background/page-hide/unmount/language paths already stop the queue. Keep those lifecycles and the existing queue/driver epoch guards; transition work is not the root-cause fix for #28.
- [App navigation](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/App.tsx#L67-L125) renders play from persisted `activeBoardId`; exit clears it without selecting that board. Thus dashboard-started/reloaded play can return to the dashboard, while editor-started play can return to the retained selection. The new handoff must always bind the active board explicitly and avoid a transient dashboard or account-entry screen.
- [BoardEditor](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/BoardEditor.tsx) already has the requested controls. At width 900 and above, preview is left and a 280-unit actions panel is right; narrower layouts stack. Retain this established placement as the starting point, use measured available space including safe areas, and allow controls to scroll in short viewports. Do not duplicate the grid planner's card distribution algorithm.
- [Web ParentControl](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/ParentControl.web.tsx) sends `click.detail === 0` directly to the dialog; [native ParentControl](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/ParentControl.tsx) does likewise for accessibility activation. This is a preventive regression concern when removing the dialog, not a claim of an observed one-tap editor defect. Check actual control bounds as well as movement distance: leaving near an edge can move less than 12 units.

**Proposed handoff**

On valid release, latch one transition, cancel the hold/contact state, stop active and pending speech, clear flash timers, and record the current board identity plus source geometry. Mount the existing editor and its controls immediately, measure its preview after any fullscreen/status-bar change, and animate an inert presentation into that target (a short approximately 200–300 ms transition is a starting point). Keep that visual layer noninteractive and hidden from accessibility. Use stable card IDs and the shared grid's final geometry; no second live editor, library copy or AI session. Rotation/resize cancels stale measurements and settles in the correct usable layout. Backgrounding never lets an incomplete hold unlock later. Once unlock has completed, an interrupted animation settles in edit rather than returning a stale hold or blank screen.

Keyboard Space/Enter down/up should use the same two-second clock and release semantics, ignore repeat events and cancel on blur/Escape. Native screen-reader interaction needs a documented deliberate equivalent using the same cancellable timing; generic activate must not directly navigate. Validate TalkBack/VoiceOver operation during implementation, without replacing access with an unusable pointer-only hold. Announce readiness and the mode change once; move focus to a non-editable editor heading, and return focus to the play heading/parent control without speaking a card. Respect runtime reduced-motion changes.

The library remains authoritative. [useLibrary](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/data/useLibrary.ts) has optimistic changes, serialized writes, durable commits, flush and retry. Retain visible edits/errors if a mode write fails; do not depend on animation completion to save. Return to play resolves the latest board and waits for required writes before displaying play. Existing card sheets and AI routes retain explicit Save/Cancel, abort and revision checks; do not expose a background return action that unmounts a draft or pending save. Preserve existing missing-voice checks, consent/disclosures, automatic-audio eligibility, protected photos and proposal validation. No new generation occurs solely because editing opens.

**Coordination**

The grid planner was contacted in its verified task about stable measured geometry and shared files. Grid-first is the recommended integration order; if stacked, the coordinator must bind the exact parent/head and refresh evidence after it changes. PR #29's account owner retains `App.tsx` ownership; its guard permits sync only outside selected/active/draft sessions, so avoid a transient idle-library window during handoff. issueComments.body:
Source request and planning findings

The human reported a good four-card 2×2 portrait layout, a 3+1 landscape layout, and requested fuller use of space with square-ish (not strictly square) cards and rows equal in count or differing by one. Exact scoping authorization: “Yeah, so spin up a task to scope that out um through planning and then create an issue”. Source coordinator task: `01a0f838-69d6-75b3-8cc0-f768175aa03e`. Its later trusted update authorizes coordinated implementation after both plans; this task only creates the plan/issue.

Inspected live master **`1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4`** on the designated ZBook; the clean local checkout matched it. No product source, branch or active worktree was changed.

- [gridLayout](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/packages/core/src/interaction.ts) tries 1–8 columns, fills a regular rectangle and scores minimum side minus aspect distortion and a small empty-slot penalty. It does not enforce balanced occupied rows. [PlayBoard](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/PlayBoard.tsx) then derives positions with modulo/division by that column count.
- [BoardEditor](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/BoardEditor.tsx) shares the helper but caps preview cells at 164×148, uses an 8-unit gap, and permits preview scrolling. Updating only the helper's column choice would leave both consumers unable to represent rows such as 4+3 with independent widths. Return ordered row/per-card geometry and adapt both consumers.
- [TouchSurface](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/TouchSurface.tsx) and its web counterpart already consume rectangles and cancel old contacts when they change. Keep stable card IDs and those interaction contracts; geometry changes should not recreate the speech queue. Preserve the editor's actions and the play header's measured space.
- Existing [unit](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/packages/core/src/interaction.test.ts) and [browser](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/tests/web/app.spec.ts) tests check fit/touch dimensions and 24-card access, but do not assert balanced occupied rows. They were read, not run.

A planning-only Node probe executed the unchanged sizing function extracted from that Git revision. Synthetic bounds subtract the current 32-unit horizontal padding and 92-unit header/bottom allocation; actual safe-area measurements and installed-build identity remain unverified:

| Viewport assumption | Board bounds | Current four-card rows | Current cell |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 820×1180 | 788×1088 | 2+2 | 388×538 |
| 1180×820 | 1148×728 | 3+1 | 374.7×358 |
| 900×600 | 868×508 | 3+1 | 281.3×248 |

This reproduces the **source-function selection**, not the user's device UI. A 192-case numerical exploration (1–24 cards at eight sizes) supports quotient/remainder row distribution; at the tablet landscape bounds, 2+2 gives 568×358 cards, while five/seven cards can use 3+2 / 4+3. Rectangles are expected: forcing squares would leave space unused. Candidate scoring still needs visual tuning—an early scalar score picked an undesirable 2+1+1 for four cards on a narrow phone. Prefer uniform rows among similarly usable options and validate boundaries, rather than copy that experiment as production code.

Very small windows expose a genuine constraint: at synthetic 288×228 board bounds, 24 cards with current gaps cannot all meet the 44-unit floor. Preserve non-scrolling play on the specified phone/tablet acceptance sizes; tiny-window behavior must be explicit rather than shrinking text/targets indefinitely. Editor preview scrolling already exists. Long labels need deliberate two-line/wrapping/truncation behavior and complete accessible names, with image space protected.

Coordination/dispositions: #30 owns navigation/animation and should follow this settled geometry; it is not a duplicate. #28's reported stuck playback remains a separate unresolved investigation. The full paginated issue/PR discussions and review/inline collections for nearby #19/#29 and #20 were retrieved; their account-entry and billing/provenance feedback stays with their existing owners, and this scoping task makes no readiness or resolution assessment. Neither PR changes the core layout, PlayBoard or BoardEditor, so neither is a prerequisite. All existing open/closed issue titles and open PR paths were checked for duplication.
